rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results (Tables 3-9) - the study reports its own field experiments on five furrow irrigation methods (conventional, surge, alternate) for grain maize in the Jayder plain, Iran, during 2021, plus WinSRFR calibration, sensitivity analysis and iso-performance optimisation of inflow rate and cutoff time.
rows.notes: The study contains no drip or drip-fertigation treatment and no nutrient measurements. It shows that variable alternate furrow irrigation (AFI) achieved the highest application efficiency (78.7%) and lowest runoff (19.5%) versus conventional furrow irrigation (62.0% AE, 35.7% runoff), and that optimising inflow rate and cutoff time with WinSRFR improved AE by up to ~8%. It provides no evidence on drip fertigation minimising surface runoff or reducing soil evaporation via buried laterals; the technology is surface furrow irrigation, not drip.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract and reference list absent but all main sections present). The study is a furrow-irrigation field/modelling study and is unrelated to the drip fertigation claim for which it is cited.
